claim: India had 2,117 GCCs in FY2026, spanning 3,728 GCC units, described as 32% growth since FY2021.
supportingEvidence: Zinnov's landscape page lists 2,117 GCCs across 3,728 units and presents this as 32% growth since FY2021. It also splits the base into 506 Forbes Global 2000 GCCs, 583 mid-market GCCs and 504 PE-backed GCCs.

claim: India had 2,117 GCCs employing 2.36 million people with revenue of USD 98.4 billion in FY2026.
supportingEvidence: YourStory's May 2026 article reports the same three headline numbers and 32% growth since FY21, attributing them to the nasscom–Zinnov report titled 'GCC Value Orbit'.

subjectLabel: India GCC employees and revenue, FY2026
claim: GCCs in India employed 2.36 million people and generated USD 98.4 billion in market revenue in FY2026.
supportingEvidence: Zinnov's page gives 2.36 million GCC employees and USD 98.4 billion market revenue for FY2026, and calls India the top AI hiring market globally.

claim: Flexiple restates 2,117 GCCs, 3,728 units, 2.36 million employees and USD 98.4 billion revenue, up from about 1.9 million employees and USD 64.6 billion in FY2024.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page repeats the Zinnov–nasscom FY2026 totals and adds FY2024 comparators for employment and revenue.
statusNote: Secondary restatement by an aggregator. The FY2026 totals match the Zinnov page, but the FY2024 comparators (1.9M employees, USD 64.6B) appear only here and were not traced to Zinnov or nasscom.

claim: Zinnov counts 506 Forbes Global 2000 GCCs, 583 mid-market GCCs and 504 PE-backed GCCs in India.
supportingEvidence: The Zinnov page breaks part of the 2,117 base into these three parent-type groups. The three groups do not sum to 2,117 on the page, so other parent types are not itemised.
statusNote: Single source (primary publisher).

claim: By maturity, Zinnov places 13% of GCCs as Outpost, 43% as Satellite, 39% as Portfolio Hub and 5% as Transformation Hub.
supportingEvidence: Zinnov's page lists this four-stage maturity distribution as context for the FY2026 landscape.
statusNote: Single source (primary publisher).

claim: More than 1,200 GCCs have embedded AI and machine-learning capabilities, with over 250 dedicated Centres of Excellence and a talent base of 250,000 AI professionals.
supportingEvidence: YourStory reports these AI figures from the nasscom–Zinnov report, and adds that nearly half of GCCs built since FY21 had AI as a core focus from inception.
statusNote: Single source; the underlying report was not opened for these specific figures.

subjectLabel: City share of India GCC office leasing, Q3 2026
claim: In Q3 2026 (CBRE data as reported), Hyderabad accounted for 37% of GCC office leasing in India, Bengaluru 28%, and Chennai and Delhi-NCR 11% each, out of about 8.7 million sq ft leased by GCCs.
supportingEvidence: Great Andhra reports CBRE's Q3 2026 figures: GCCs leased about 8.7 million sq ft nationally, with the city shares above. Pune and Mumbai are described only as having smaller shares, with no figures given.
statusNote: Relayed from CBRE by a news outlet; the CBRE release was not opened. The remainder (13%) in the chart is derived by subtraction and is not reported by the source.

subjectLabel: GCC share of India office take-up, Q3 2026
claim: GCCs took about 41% of India's office take-up in Q3 2026 and about 42% across the first nine months (CBRE data as reported).
supportingEvidence: Great Andhra reports national Q3 absorption of about 21 million sq ft, up 6% year on year, with GCC leasing of about 8.7 million sq ft.
statusNote: Relayed from CBRE by a news outlet.

subjectLabel: GCC share of India office take-up, Q2 2026
claim: GCCs accounted for 42% of India's Q2 2026 office take-up, with GCC leasing at an all-time high of 10.3 million sq ft and a 43% share of H1 demand (CBRE data as reported).
supportingEvidence: Business Standard's July 2026 article reports CBRE's Q2 figures for record gross leasing driven by GCC and flex demand.
statusNote: Relayed from CBRE by a news outlet; the CBRE release was not opened.

claim: Eli Lilly announced a second India capability centre, Lilly Capability Centre India, in Hyderabad, recruiting 1,000–1,500 people, alongside its existing Bengaluru centre.
supportingEvidence: Fierce Pharma (10 Jan 2025), citing a Lilly release, says the Hyderabad centre was expected to become operational in mid-2025 and is hiring technology engineers and data scientists for automation, AI, software product engineering and cloud. No investment figure or state-government source is cited.
statusNote: Single source. Announcement verified; operational status after mid-2025 was not checked.

claim: Vanguard announced a GCC in Hyderabad to hire about 2,300 people over four years for technology roles in AI, data and analytics, and mobile engineering.
supportingEvidence: Deccan Chronicle (31 Mar 2025) reports Vanguard's decision after a meeting with Telangana's Chief Minister, who welcomed it. The office was due to open formally later in 2025. No investment figure is stated.
statusNote: Single source. Other outlets' headlines in search listings cite different totals (about 2,400–2,500); these were not opened and the figure is not reconciled with a Vanguard release.

subjectLabel: Amgen – Hyderabad technology and innovation site
claim: Amgen announced a technology and innovation site in HITEC City, Hyderabad, to employ up to 3,000 people.
supportingEvidence: BioSpectrum India (9 Aug 2024) says the site would initially build digital capabilities and technology solutions, with roles later covering AI, data science and life sciences, and was slated to be operational in Q4 2024. No investment figure is stated.
statusNote: Single source. Announcement verified; operational status was not checked.

subjectLabel: McDonald's – Hyderabad India office and GCC
claim: McDonald's plans an India office and a GCC in Hyderabad, with an initial headcount of 2,000 for the India office.
supportingEvidence: The News Minute (19 Mar 2025) reports details from Telangana's Chief Minister's office after a meeting with McDonald's chairman and CEO, saying the company will also use Telangana as a skilling zone. The article does not specify the GCC's functions.
statusNote: Single source relaying the state government's account; no McDonald's statement was retrieved.

claim: Rolls-Royce opened what it calls its largest global capability and innovation centre, in Manyata Embassy Business Park, Bengaluru, with 700 seats.
supportingEvidence: The People's Board (18 Sep 2025) says Karnataka's Large and Medium Industries Minister inaugurated the centre, and that Rolls-Royce has more than 3,000 staff in India, over 2,000 of them skilled engineers in Karnataka. Specific functions and investment are not stated.
statusNote: Single source (trade press).

claim: DePuy Synthes, the orthopaedics business of Johnson & Johnson MedTech, plans a Bengaluru GCC hiring about 500 professionals over 18–24 months.
supportingEvidence: Indian Pharma Post (8 Aug 2026) lists software engineering, data and AI, enterprise applications, technology services and cybersecurity among the functions, and quotes DePuy Synthes's worldwide president on India's orthopaedic market.
statusNote: Single source (trade press).

claim: Mizuho Financial Group launched Mizuho Global Services India Pvt. Ltd., a technology and operations centre in Pune.
supportingEvidence: Mizuho's own press release (dateline 20 May 2026) says the centre brings together technology, operations and business-services staff to support round-the-clock global operations. Headcount and investment are not stated.
statusNote: Single source, but it is the company's own press release.

subjectLabel: The Magnum Ice Cream Company – Pune GCC
claim: The Magnum Ice Cream Company inaugurated a GCC in Pune covering finance, procurement, supply chain, marketing and master data, with a focus on AI, automation and analytics.
supportingEvidence: The company's newsroom (4 Sep 2026) also mentions an April 2025 MoU with the Government of Maharashtra, without a monetary value, and says Maharashtra holds two-thirds of its India workforce. No GCC headcount or investment is stated.
statusNote: Single source, but it is the company's own newsroom.

subjectLabel: KLA – Chennai R&D and innovation hub
claim: KLA unveiled an INR 300 crore R&D and innovation hub in Chennai designed for up to 1,300 employees, working on AI, software development, engineering and product support.
supportingEvidence: Voice&Data (7 Jan 2026) describes the facility as a research and development and innovation hub. It does not describe it as a GCC.
statusNote: Facility details verified in one trade source. Classification as a GCC is not stated there. A Feb 2026 search listing headlines a USD 400 million Chennai campus; it was not opened, so the two figures are not reconciled.

subjectLabel: KLA – Chennai land for GCC and R&D facility
claim: KLA has acquired over 12 acres on the Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam corridor in Chennai for a GCC and R&D facility.
supportingEvidence: DT Next (updated 7 Sep 2026) mentions the land purchase while describing Tamil Nadu's GCC corridor programme, and is the only fetched source that links KLA's Chennai facility to the term GCC.
statusNote: Incidental mention in an article about the corridor programme.

claim: Starbucks signed an MoU with the Tamil Nadu government to open its first India GCC in Chennai, with over 800 technology jobs.
supportingEvidence: Deccan Chronicle (ANI, 21 Sep 2026) says the centre operates independently of Starbucks' retail joint venture with Tata Consumer Products and cites the state Industries department for the job figure. Functions and investment are not stated.
statusNote: Single source (wire report). This is an MoU, not an operating centre.

claim: Walgreens plans a GCC in Chennai focused on technology and business services, expected to create more than 250 jobs in its first year.
supportingEvidence: Medical Dialogues (Reuters-sourced, 18 Sep 2026) attributes the details to an unnamed statement and refers to a pact with Walgreens India. It does not mention a Tamil Nadu government MoU. Investment is not stated.
statusNote: Single source; the issuer of the underlying statement is not named in the article.

claim: JLL India (Feb 2026) puts Bengaluru at over 900 GCC units and 34–39% of India's GCC market.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page lists these figures in its city table and attributes them to JLL India.
statusNote: Relayed from JLL by an aggregator; the JLL report was not opened. 'GCC market' is not defined on the page.

claim: The Government of Karnataka's IT department is cited as reporting over 500 GCCs in the state, about 35% of India's GCC workforce, and over 600,000 GCC employees.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page lists these figures for Karnataka (2026) and attributes them to the Government of Karnataka's Department of Electronics, IT and BT.
statusNote: State-level, not city-level. Relayed by an aggregator; the Karnataka source was not opened.

claim: Hyderabad is cited at about 20% of India's GCCs, with 40 new GCCs in 2025 through October, the most of any Indian city; JLL India separately puts it at 20–23% of GCC office demand over 2022–2025.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page attributes the first figures to the Telangana Socio Economic Outlook 2026 (via Deccan Chronicle) and the second to JLL India.
statusNote: Relayed secondhand; neither the Outlook nor the JLL report was opened. Count-based and demand-based shares are different measures.

claim: JLL India puts Pune at 15–20% of national GCC activity over 2022–2025.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page lists this range for Pune and attributes it to JLL India. 'Activity' is not defined on the page.
statusNote: Relayed from JLL by an aggregator; the JLL report was not opened.

claim: Flexiple's own tracked-professional counts are Bangalore 7.1M+, Hyderabad 5.3M+, Chennai 4.1M+ and Pune 2.4M+ (as of Aug 2026).
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page presents these as its own dataset of tracked professionals across six metros, explicitly separate from GCC counts.
statusNote: Platform-specific dataset, not a labour-market statistic. Useful only as a rough relative indicator.

claim: No verifiable city-level GCC count for Chennai was found; the only source for it cites no underlying data.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page states that Chennai, Mumbai and Delhi NCR GCC counts cannot be verified because the only available source cites no underlying data.
statusNote: This record documents a gap rather than a figure.

claim: Telangana is reported to have crossed 500 GCCs after adding 75 in 2025–26, with a target of 100 more this financial year, about 55 already set up in Hyderabad.
supportingEvidence: Siasat Daily (17 Sep 2026), citing The Times of India and officials, gives these figures alongside a 1 lakh direct and 3 lakh indirect jobs target from the state's IT and Industries Minister.
statusNote: State-level counts reported by a news outlet citing another outlet and officials.

claim: CBRE Q3 2026 (as reported): Hyderabad absorbed about 5.3M sq ft with about 10.2M sq ft of new supply; Bengaluru about 4.9M sq ft absorbed with about 3.9M sq ft of supply; Pune had about 2.7M sq ft of completions; no Chennai or Pune absorption figure was given.
supportingEvidence: Great Andhra's 2 Oct 2026 article gives these CBRE figures and notes that Hyderabad has the largest new supply of the cities it cites.
statusNote: Relayed from CBRE by a news outlet; the CBRE release was not opened. Office space is a proxy for infrastructure, not a full measure.

claim: Colliers' Q3 2026 framework (as reported) shows Bengaluru leading with 5.2M sq ft of Grade-A gross absorption versus 2.2M sq ft for Hyderabad, the reverse of CBRE's ranking.
supportingEvidence: Great Andhra's article notes that Colliers uses a different methodology from CBRE, which explains why the two firms' city orderings differ.
statusNote: Methodology conflict between CBRE and Colliers is unresolved. Do not rank cities from either series alone.

claim: GCCs made up 55% of Chennai's office leasing in Q1 2026 (Cushman & Wakefield), and Chennai's GCC leasing grew more than four-fold in 2025 versus 2021 (Colliers), as reported.
supportingEvidence: DT Next (updated 7 Sep 2026) cites both figures while covering the state's GCC corridor programme.
statusNote: Third-party figures relayed by a news outlet; the originating reports were not opened.

claim: Tamil Nadu unveiled a GCC Corridor and Development Programme covering three Chennai corridors (Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road, Mount–Poonamallee High Road and OMR) with enhanced floor space index and shared infrastructure.
supportingEvidence: DT Next (updated 7 Sep 2026) reports the Industries Minister announced the programme in a social-media post. The article does not say whether it has been formally adopted or is in effect.
statusNote: Announcement via social media as reported; no official programme document located.

claim: Maharashtra's GCC Policy 2025 (GR dated 3 Nov 2025, Industries, Energy, Labour & Mining Dept) runs to the end of FY2029–30, targets about 400 new GCCs and 400,000 high-skilled jobs, and sets five eligibility tiers by fixed capital investment and employees.
supportingEvidence: The official GR lists tiers from Small (Rs 50–100 crore, 100–250 employees) to Ultra-large (above Rs 750 crore, over 1,000 employees) and a budget of Rs 2,960 crore for 2025–30.
statusNote: Official government document.

subjectLabel: Maharashtra GCC Policy 2025 – capital and operating subsidies
claim: The policy offers a capital subsidy of 20% of eligible investment capped at Rs 10 crore (small) to Rs 100 crore (very large), rent subsidy, power tariff subsidy, and a 10-year electricity duty exemption.
supportingEvidence: The GR specifies capital subsidy in five instalments, a Zone 1 rent subsidy of 10% for five years capped at Rs 1–4 crore by tier, power tariff subsidy of Rs 1 per unit for five years in Zone 1, and stamp duty concessions via MAITS 2023 with no percentage given.
statusNote: Official government document.

claim: The Pune Metropolitan Region is in Zone 1, which gets a 40% payroll subsidy on salary above Rs 1 lakh per month (up to Rs 50,000 per employee for 3 years) but a lower rent subsidy than Zone 2, no interest subsidy, and a lower power subsidy.
supportingEvidence: The GR caps the payroll subsidy at 100 employees per GCC per year and Rs 5 crore per company per year, adds 10% where at least half the hires are women or persons with disabilities, and names Mumbai and Pune as the main GCC park hubs.
statusNote: Official government document.

claim: Per a law-firm summary, Karnataka's final GCC Policy 2024–29 (released 19 Nov 2024) funds innovation labs and CoEs in Bengaluru Urban at INR 5 crore capped at two projects a year, reimburses internet costs up to INR 12 lakh a year for three years, and reimburses facility and lab usage costs after six months.
supportingEvidence: Khaitan & Co's 2 Dec 2024 alert also describes 'Beyond Bengaluru' incentives (75% funding capped at INR 3 crore, five years of electricity duty reimbursement, 10% recruitment-cost support for expansions of 100+ employees) and open skilling incentives.
statusNote: Law-firm summary only. The official policy text was not located; validate amounts and eligibility against it.

claim: Flexiple lists Karnataka's 2024–29 GCC policy targets as 500 new centres, 350,000 new jobs and USD 50 billion of economic output, attributed to the Government of Karnataka.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's statistics page gives these targets in its state-policy section. Search listings from other outlets show a different jobs figure ('35 lakh') that was not opened.
statusNote: Jobs target conflicts across listings; confirm against the official policy.

claim: Telangana is reported (17 Sep 2026) to be preparing a new GCC policy focused on space, semiconductors, AI, quantum and advanced life sciences, steering new centres toward tier-2 towns; no incentive amounts are given.
supportingEvidence: Siasat Daily, citing The Times of India and officials involved in drafting, says the state is studying Karnataka's and Maharashtra's GCC policies and that incentives would go to investments that build entirely new ecosystems.
statusNote: Draft status per a news report; no official document located. Existing ICT-policy incentives were not researched.

subjectLabel: Tamil Nadu payroll subsidy for GCCs (budget announcement)
claim: Tamil Nadu's 2024–25 budget announced a payroll subsidy for new GCC jobs paying above Rs 1 lakh a month, at 30% in year one, 20% in year two and 10% in year three.
supportingEvidence: DT Next (updated 19 Feb 2024) reports the rates and the stated aim of making Tamil Nadu the prime destination for GCCs. It does not give a target number of GCCs.
statusNote: Budget announcement as reported; the operating government order was not located.

subjectLabel: Tamil Nadu Payroll Incentive Scheme (agency page)
claim: Guidance Tamil Nadu lists a Payroll Incentive Scheme that subsidises salaries for new high-paying jobs to anchor GCCs, without giving amounts, eligibility or duration.
supportingEvidence: The agency's policy page names the scheme under notable policy initiatives, alongside a GCC policy described only as one of the state's recent sector policies.
statusNote: Verifies that the scheme exists; amounts are not on this page.

subjectLabel: Tamil Nadu payroll subsidy – duration and target (secondary)
claim: Flexiple lists Tamil Nadu's 2024–25 budget payroll subsidy as running to March 2027 and aimed at 50 GCCs, with no headline total.
supportingEvidence: Flexiple's state-policy section attributes these details to the Tamil Nadu 2024–25 budget.
statusNote: Secondary summary only; the 50-GCC target is not in the DT Next article that was opened.
